title: Full AES-192 four-related-key boomerang recovery

target.description: Full12-round AES-192 including initial whitening and the standard final round, as targeted by Section3/Figure8.

setting.key_relation: Section3.1/Figure7 and AppendixA Table2: from kA impose the selected difference on the second expanded-key subkey to generate kB; impose the eighth-subkey difference on kA/kB to generate kC/kD. These are six-column AES-192 key-expansion blocks, not ordinary 128-bit round-key indices. The probability-one key-schedule boomerang preserves the matching second-subkey differences. This is an oracle-side, key-dependent generation algorithm, not a fixed known master-key XOR relation.
setting.key_population: General unknown target key under the specified algorithmic related-key functions; no weak-key target promise is stated.
setting.plaintext_model: Decrypt structured ciphertexts under kA/kC, then adaptively encrypt paired plaintexts under kB/kD.
assumptions: Both related-key encryption and decryption access are required by Steps1–5.
The key-schedule-induced quartet construction and source boomerang compatibility assumptions are retained.
The recovered28-byte intermediate sequence is not the whole key; the source prices a further2^104 key-completion search.

time.note: Section3.2 sums message processing and counter updates using its native cost model. Additional2^104 candidate completion is lower order; not silently normalized to exact full AES encryption equivalents.

data.note: Total across4keys: kA/kC ciphertext queries and kB/kD adaptive plaintext queries; not2^124 perkey.

memory.note: A2^55-message hash table plus2^79 sequences of28bytes; source native128-bit-block estimate.

preprocessing.note: No separately itemized reusable preprocessing budget is given for this configuration; unknown does not mean zero.

success.description: Section3.2 repeats until a counter reaches2 and prices about2^69 structures, expecting two useful quartets. It does not give the probability of recovery within that fixed budget, nor the stopping-time distribution. Key-schedule construction probability1, internal boomerang probability and wrong-candidate filtering remain distinct from full-key success; a further2^104 completion is required. Section4.3 computes average transition probabilities without generally quantifying the probability of a nonzero trail.

review.scope: Targeted exact-edition success audit of defining construction and parameter passages, not a new full-paper or forward-literature audit. Source local/conditional models, expected counts, key-relation construction and full recovery remain separate.

components.description: PDF9 Section3.1: the constructed key-schedule boomerang closes with probability1 under the stated subkey-induced relations. This says nothing about the state trail or full recovery and is not a fixed master-key XOR relation.
